Prompt 1 (Version 1):

Create a complete HTML memory matching game with a 4x4 grid of 16 cards and 8 pairs. When a player clicks a card, it should flip over to reveal an icon . Players need to find matching pairs by clicking the cards. If the two cards match, they still flipped. If they don't match, they flip back again. Include embedded CSS to style an arcade station and use embedded JavaScript for all the game logic. When all pairs are matched, a message saying "You did it" show up and change colors.

Part 2Testing Documentation

Version tested: memory_game_v1.html

Section A: What Works Well

  • Individual cards flip when clicked
  • When I find a pair of cards they stay face-up
  • When I click in a non-matching card it flip back
  • When I complete all pairs it shows a message saying: You did it!
  • If I click in an already face-up card it stays face-up

Section B: Issues and Desired Improvements

  1. When I finish the game there is no way to restart the game without refreshing the page. Need to include a button to restart the game or reset it.
  2. I want to ask for a player name, so it can feel more personalized
  3. I want to change the look and feel of the game to make it more appealing. I want the game to reflect the Lord of the Rings theme, like icons or names that the player can remember from the movies.
  4. I want to have a counter every time the player clicks on a card, so it can become more challenging having numbers to improve. For me, having a number to beat makes it funnier.
  5. Include a timer so I can have another way to track the player. Having an elapsed time counter can make the game a little more fun.

Part 3Iterative Improvements

Version 2: Enhanced Functionality

Prompt 2 (Version 2):

I want you to create a complete HTML memory matching game with a 4x4 grid of 16 cards and 8 pairs. When a player clicks a card, it should flip over to reveal a character. Players need to find matching pairs by clicking the cards. If the two cards match, they stay flipped. If they don't match, they flip back again. Before the game starts, show a field asking for the player's name so the game feels personal, and use that name in the game, for example in the scoreboard and the win message. Show a move counter, a score tracker, and a timer that shows the elapsed time while the player is playing. Add a restart button that reshuffles the cards and starts a new game so it not the same every time, and a reset button that clears everything, including the score and the player's name. For the card faces, use famous Lord of the Rings characters instead of generic icons. The style should have a Middle earth feel, with the colors, fonts and card design inspired by the movies. When all pairs are matched, show a styled win display that congratulates the player by name and shows their final time, moves and score, and change the colors of the page. Use embedded CSS and embedded JavaScript for everything. I need the complete HTML file as the result.

AI Response 2: memory_game_v2.html ↗

File saved as: memory_game_v2.html

My answer (Version 2 testing):
  1. All features from version 1 still working. I kept all of them in this new version.
  2. I added some new features:
    1. A welcome screen that asks for a name before game start. This is so the game can feel more personalized. The name will also appear in the win message.
    2. A move counter, score an timer. The move counter increase every time two cards are flipped. The score add 100 points per matched pair and -10 points per miss. The timer starts on the first flip and stops when the player wins.
    3. A Restart button: starts a new game and reshuffles the cards while keeping the same player name.
    4. A Reset button: clears the score, moves counter, time and player name. Take the player to the name screen.
    5. Added a Middle Earth style, with fonts, and back card design with the Ring from the Movie.
    6. Win display: The end screen congratulates the player by name and shows the finals scores. The page colors will shift to green and gold to animate the win screen.

Version 3: Advanced Features

Prompt 3 (Version 3):

I want you to create a complete HTML memory matching game. When a player clicks a card, it should flip over to reveal a character. Players need to find matching pairs by clicking the cards. If the two cards match, they stay flipped. If they don't match, they flip back again. Before the game starts, show a screen where the player types their name, so the game feels personal, and use that name in the scoreboard and the win message. On that same screen, let the player choose a theme and a difficulty.

There are three themes to choose from: Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones. Each theme should use famous characters, creatures or symbols from that universe on the card faces, and it should have its own colors, fonts, backgrounds and card design inspired by the movies or the series. Make sure each theme has enough different characters for the biggest board. And there are three difficulty levels: Easy is a 4x4 grid, Medium is a 6x6 grid and Hard is an 8x8 grid. The grid should adjust to the screen so it.

Show a move counter, a score tracker and a timer that shows the elapsed time while the player is playing. Add a restart button that reshuffles the cards and starts a new game so it's not the same every time, and a reset button that clears everything, including the score and the player's name, and takes the player back to the first screen. The player should also be able to go back and change the theme or the difficulty without reloading the page. Add sound effects for a match, a mismatch, and winning the game and there should be a button to mute or unmute them. Add high scores with the player's name. Keep two separate lists: one for the fastest times and one for the fewest moves. Keep them separate for each difficulty and save them in the browser so they are still there when the page is opened again. Show the top 5 of each list in a nice looking board that the player can open at any time.

When the game ends, give the player a star rating from 1 to 5 stars based on their performance, using the time and the number of moves for that difficulty. Show a styled win display that congratulates the player by name and shows the final time, moves, score and stars. Also tell the player if they made it into the high scores. Change the colors of the page to celebrate and add special animations like confetti or particle effects. The animations should match the theme that is being played.

The visual design should look professional, with gradients, shadows, glow effects and smooth card flip animations. Every theme should feel different from the others, but the layout should stay clean and easy to use. Use embedded CSS and embedded JavaScript for everything. I need the complete HTML file as the result.

AI Response 3: memory_game_v3.html ↗

File saved as: memory_game_v3.html

My answer (Version 3 testing):
  1. All features from version 2 still working. I kept all of them in this new version.
  2. I added some new features:
    1. The welcome screen asks for the player's name. The name will also appear in the scoreboard, the subtitle and the win message.
    2. New Themes: The same welcome screen let the player choose among Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones.
    3. Difficulty: the easy level is a 4x4 board, medium is 6x6 and Hard is 8x8.
    4. More ways to score: score is +100 per match, with +25 extra for each match in a row and a miss costs 10 points.
    5. Sound Effects: match, mismatch and win sounds are generated in code. It also has a mute button (🔊).
    6. High Scores: there are two list, one with fastest times and another with fewer moves. The scores are saved in the browser, and the reset does not erase high scores.
    7. Animation and Visuals: each match fives a particle burst and winning fires confetti cannons and falling effect. The effect tries to match the theme of the game.

My answer (gameplay observations):

Adding a timer makes the game feel more professional. I also think a sound effect makes flipping and matching even more exciting. The hard level feels a bit overwhelming since there are so many cards to remember that I struggled at first, even when I didn't documented my play. I shared it with a coworker, and she really enjoyed it; she played a few rounds and chose Hermione as her name. It was a lot of fun!

Part 5Written Reflection

  1. Prompt Evolution: Reading the last prompt and comparing it with the first one, it is evident that the details make a big difference. Although I could see that even with how vague my first prompt was, the AI made the effort to assume some features and give me back a game that could be played. And even now, when I see the result of prompt number 3, I realize that there are still more things I would like to add or features that I could modify. I also think that each interaction helps me understand how to best specify what I want to get as a final product.
  2. AI Accuracy: This point is interesting because even with the first prompt, vague as it was, the AI's response was good enough to assume the correct behavior of the game. I didn't find any of the errors that were cited as examples in the assignment. Now that I use Claude I feel a little more confident with the results. And even so, when I tried it, I didn't find any errors that I could identify. My first experiences at the beginning of the course with Copilot had quite a few logic errors and I think this model works better.
  3. Code Understanding: Looking at the code it is quite clear how the HTML structures the page, the CSS gives it the style and JS provides the logic of the program. Before this exercise I thought it was necessary to have a separate folder for JS and CSS but I have learned how these can integrate an HTML that contains all three.
  4. AI Limitations: I couldn't identify any limitations in terms of the responses I got. I think in terms of creating the code, he did it well and delivered everything I asked for and in the way I asked for it.
  5. Learning Process: I was very surprised at how quickly each of the versions of the game were generated. I spent more time on this documentation than I did on creating the prompts I used and the AI responses. I was also very surprised at how she was able to evaluate the features of each of the themes I asked her to create on her own. How she chose appropriate icons and even the effects at the end of the winner screen.
  6. Future Use: I must admit that the ease I have found for the generation of an application like this opens up a whole world of possibilities for the search for practical solutions in my work. I believe that I will use AI to generate the logical basis for some routine tasks in my work. I believe that AI programs in one way and I do it in another. I believe that my contribution in these future tests that I will do in my work will be that of logic and how I want it to solve it, beyond just stating the need and waiting for it to find the solution. I really liked this exercise. I see this as a great opportunity to put into practice the skills that I am developing in prompting.
